claim: A floor-aligned sprite lays its tile WIDTH along (-sin a, cos a) and its HEIGHT along (-cos a, -sin a): at angle 0 the tile's x runs along map +y, not +x. Its size is texels x repeat / 4, and art picanm offsets and the sprite's own offsets move its centre.
evidence: NBlood/source/build/src/engine_priv.h:479-493 get_floorspr_points (x2 = x1 - sin*span.x, y2 = y1 + cos*span.x).
A carriage roof written at angle 0 assuming tile x = map x lay 768 x 1024 per piece: gaps along the car and overhangs; the renderer showed them as dark bands, read at first as beams (2026-11-19).
use: Never size or place a floor sprite by hand: bloodmap.flatsprite.cover tiles a rectangle exactly, footprint/box say where one lies, faults proves a set covers with nothing bare or doubled. A regular pattern on a surface built of sprites is a fault until measured.
